catalog_locator: Fleming & Dennis 1977:127, quoted in Garrett ROA-1031 sec. 3.3 (p.16, table (27) and following paragraph)
catalog_quote: (27) Languages with exceptional final stress ... Tol (Hokan, Honduras) final if CVC, else penultimate CV (Fleming and Dennis 1977) ... Take an example: in Tol, “in a majority of cases, stress occurs on the final syllable of consonant-final words [phesmás ‘skunk’] and the penultimate syllable of vowel-final words [phésme ‘skunk’] ... However, stress may also occur on the final syllable of vowel final words [?isí ‘water’, chiyó ‘dog’] and, less frequently, on the penultimate syllable of consonant-final words” (Fleming and Dennis 1977, p. 127). Long vowels do not occur, but CV monosyllables are allowed: tI ‘heavy’ p. 121, pi ‘buttocks’, pe ‘rock’ p. 122.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the Garrett ROA-1031 PDF we hold (sec. 3.3, p.17; record says p.16, off by one), and it is explicitly a carry of Fleming & Dennis 1977:127, which we do not hold. The held Dennis & Dennis 1983 dictionary appendix (p.57) independently confirms the same default as an orthographic rule (unaccented words: final stress if consonant-final, penult if vowel-final; accent written otherwise), so the majority rule is not in doubt. sources.note: Maddieson's three-way tone typology codes Tol as 'No tones', citing Fleming and Dennis 1977 and Holt 1999a; a second-hand but explicit statement that Tol has no lexical/grammatical tone, consistent with the primary sources describing only a stress phoneme. Our packet/copy had WALS 14A-17A (stress) for Tol but not 13A.

sources.note: Slides 17-19 give the vowel system (6 vowels; /ɨ/ back unrounded per Holt 1999, central per Hernández 2022) and the consonant system (plain/aspirated/glottalized stops and affricates, fricatives, nasals, lateral, glides per Hernández vs Holt); no slide on stress, tone or prosody; slides 26-34 are a full Tol bibliography (major grammars: Hernández 2022, Holt 1999, Haurholm-Larsen & Pynes ms; SIL works; UNAH student theses 1983-2022).
